description:
## Outcome

One reusable harness unpacks a target archive in an isolated test root and verifies the packaged product without Erlang or Elixir on `PATH`. It also records startup time from the final archive bytes.

## Work

1. Accept an archive, expected target, and expected version as explicit inputs.
2. Unpack under a path with spaces and under a non-ASCII profile path.
3. Build a minimal `PATH` with no system `erl`, `elixir`, or `mix`, and prove the launcher still runs.
4. Check version and help commands, a provider-free local scenario, exit statuses `0`, `1`, and `64`, daemon lifecycle, restart persistence, and no-daemon behavior.
5. Measure 20 warm runs and one cold run for help, version, first TUI frame, and runtime-ready state.
6. Gate the warm medians at 0.50 seconds for help and version, 0.50 seconds for the first frame, and 1.25 seconds for runtime ready.
7. Prove that the first frame appears before runtime-ready state. Send input during startup and prove one queued submission runs exactly once after ready.
8. Validate layout, metadata, notices, file permissions or access controls, private runtime selection, packaged `priv` data, and native libraries.
9. Capture diagnostics separately and reject unexpected secret or host-path data.
10. Emit machine-readable test and performance evidence for CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same harness runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- [ ] It fails if the launcher finds a system OTP or misses packaged runtime data.
- [ ] It fails when a warm startup median exceeds a release limit.
- [ ] It records cold startup and the 95th percentile without using the cold result as a first-release gate.
- [ ] It fails on a partial JSONL line or an ambiguous local run artifact state.
- [ ] It never calls a live model provider.
- [ ] It distinguishes automated first-frame checks from the manual TUI checklist.
- [ ] Failures identify the target and exact acceptance check.

## Tests

Test the harness with known-good synthetic packages and packages with removed runtime, bad metadata, bad permissions, corrupt JSONL, wrong exits, delayed paint, delayed readiness, and duplicate queued submission.

## Non-goals

Do not duplicate the local output-directory lifecycle owned by `jido_cli-tqg.6.4`. Do not claim that a pseudo-terminal is full TUI acceptance.
title: Build a hermetic packaged-artifact acceptance harness
